title: Kenyan Coconut Potatoes
community: Swahili — a beloved coastal side dish
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Viazi vya Nazi — potatoes simmered in a fragrant coconut milk sauce with onions, tomatoes, turmeric, and fresh coriander. A simple, creamy, and deeply comforting coastal Kenyan side dish that transforms humble potatoes into something beautiful.
longDesc: Coconut potatoes are one of those dishes that demonstrate what makes Swahili cooking so special — the addition of coconut milk to a simple potato and tomato stew creates something creamy, fragrant, and utterly satisfying. It is a classic coastal side dish served alongside grilled fish, chicken curries, or simply on its own with chapati.
ingredients: 600g potatoes — peeled and cut into chunks
steps: Heat oil. Cook onions until soft and golden — 6 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger. Cook 30 seconds.
Add tomatoes, turmeric, curry powder, and paprika. Cook for 6—8 minutes until thick.
Add potato chunks. Stir to coat in the spiced sauce.
Pour in coconut milk. Stir gently.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover and cook for 15—20 minutes until potatoes are completely tender.
Do not boil hard — coconut milk splits.
chefTips: Cut potatoes into even chunks for uniform cooking.
Never boil vigorously after adding coconut milk.
Slightly mash a few potato pieces to thicken the sauce naturally.
commonMistakes: Uneven potato sizes — some raw, some overcooked.

faqs.a: Yes — sweet potato, carrot, or peas can be added. Sweet potato is particularly good and very popular along the coast.

cookingScience: Potato starch dissolves slightly into the coconut milk during cooking, naturally thickening the sauce without any additional thickeners.
reheating: Gently on stovetop with a splash of coconut milk.
healthBenefits: Potatoes provide potassium and vitamin C.
culturalNote: Viazi vya Nazi is a beloved everyday dish along Kenya's Swahili coast — the coconut milk elevating simple potatoes into a distinctly coastal preparation that pairs beautifully with the region's grilled fish and seafood.
